A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VMAE/LDMAE research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, latent-space, efficiency, image-generation, and loss-ablation results in Sections 5–6, Tables 1–4, and associated figures.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including reconstruction and generation comparisons, noise-perturbation experiments, and loss ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions propose the same symmetric ViT-based VMAE with masking, reconstruction, perceptual, and KL regularization losses. Appendix B.1 in v3 supplies architectural details without reporting a change to the method.

E1.justification: Both use ImageNet-1K for autoencoder training and class-conditional generation, CelebA-HQ for unconditional generation, and ADE20K/CelebAMask-HQ for object-level and part-level compression evaluation. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated AE, DAE, VAE, and SD-VAE comparators remain unchanged in Tables 1–3 and the latent-space analyses. v3 removes a redundant baseline list from Section 5, but retains those methods in the comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported datasets, metrics, learning rates, batch sizes, DiT-B/1 backbone, 100K/60K training iterations, and 250-step Euler sampling remain unchanged. Newly specified VMAE architecture settings in Appendix B.1 are disclosures, with no stated revision to existing settings.

E4.justification: The noise-perturbation analysis, feature-clustering and compression analyses, reconstruction examples, and cumulative loss ablation in Table 4 are retained. The appendices contain the same generation examples, without additional analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain point-estimate reporting. Neither supplies experimental seed lists, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All values in Tables 1–4 and the plotted results are unchanged. For example, VMAE retains reconstruction rFID 0.89 and generation gFID 5.98 on ImageNet-1K and 7.61 on CelebA-HQ. Main-text and appendix sample images also match.

T1.justification: The diffusion objectives, Equations (1)–(7), and compression/disentanglement definitions remain unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and summary retain the same three desired autoencoder properties, VMAE/LDMAE contributions, and claimed generation-quality and efficiency advantages.

C2.justification: v3 trims repeated latent-smoothness explanations but retains their meaning elsewhere. Interpretations linking probabilistic latents, hierarchical compression, reconstruction, and generation quality remain unchanged, as do the stated applicability arguments.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link in the abstract. Appendix B.1 newly specifies 32×32 patches, embedding dimension 192, masking ratio 0.6, 12 encoder and 12 decoder Transformer layers, and decoder mask-token handling. These improve documentation of the existing model.

R1.justification: v3 adds Choi et al.'s work on GAN latent manifolds in Section 4.1 and Hahm et al.'s work on isometric diffusion representations in Section 4.2. These supplement existing motivations without substantially changing research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammar corrections, removes redundant passages, expands Appendix B.1, and adds acknowledgments. The section organization and central narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 3 and 4 are rearranged on the generation-results page, and appendix Figure I moves from a page shared with implementation details to a separate page. Figures and table structures are retained; Figure II also corrects 'Huskey' to 'Husky.'

improvement.justification: v3 reduces reproduction ambiguity through previously unspecified architecture settings in Appendix B.1 and a code-access pointer. Small language and citation improvements also help. These are useful documentation gains, while the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
